content: 1. Administer 5 mg/kg of the drug every 8 hours. After discharge, continue treatment with doxycycline 100 mg orally every 12 hours to complete a 14-day therapy course. 2. Administer 900 mg intravenously every 8 hours, combined with oxacillin or nafcillin (2 g intravenously every 4 hours) or vancomycin (30 mg/kg/day intravenously divided every 12 hours). 3. Administer 600 mg orally, intravenously, or intramuscularly 30–60 minutes before a procedure. Avoid intramuscular injections in patients receiving anticoagulant therapy; use oral administration in such cases. Intravenous administration should only be used if the patient cannot tolerate or absorb oral medications. 4. Administer 600 mg intravenously or orally every 6 hours for at least 6 weeks. 5. For oral administration, give 300 mg orally every 12 hours for 7 days. 6. Administer 30 mg/kg/day divided every 6–8 hours. Alternatively, administer 300–450 mg orally every 6–8 hours with primaquine for 21 days, or 600–900 mg intravenously every 6–8 hours with primaquine for 21 days. 7. Oral administration may be taken with food. 8. For intravenous administration, give 15–40 mg/kg/day divided every 6–8 hours. For oral administration, give 8–25 mg/kg/day divided every 6–8 hours. 9. For prophylaxis, administer 20 mg/kg orally 30–60 minutes before a procedure, or 20 mg/kg intravenously or intramuscularly within 30–60 minutes before a procedure. 10. Consider use in patients allergic to penicillin, as per IDSA guidelines. 11. For chronic carrier treatment, administer 20–30 mg/kg/day orally divided every 8 hours, not exceeding 300 mg per dose. 12. For acute treatment in penicillin-allergic patients, administer 7 mg/kg per dose three times daily for 10 days, not exceeding 300 mg per dose. 13. Administer 10–20 mg/kg/day orally divided every 6–8 hours, or 15–25 mg/kg/day intravenously divided every 6–8 hours. Adjust the dose as necessary, but do not exceed 40 mg/kg/day. 14. For intramuscular administration, do not exceed 600 mg per injection. 15. For endocarditis, recent AHA guidelines recommend prophylaxis only for invasive procedures in high-risk patients. Oral administration may be taken with food. 16. Clindamycin increases the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 17. Clindamycin decreases the effects of the BCG live vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is contraindicated; wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 18. Clindamycin decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 19. Clindamycin increases the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 20. Clindamycin decreases the effects of microbiota oral therapy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 21. Clindamycin increases the effects of pancuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 22. Clindamycin increases the effects of rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 23. Clindamycin increases the effects of rocuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 24. Clindamycin increases the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 25. Clindamycin decreases the effects of the typhoid live vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is contraindicated; wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 26. Clindamycin increases the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 27. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens, estradiol, ethinyl estradiol, and other hormonal contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. Consider using an alternative or additional form of birth control during concomitant use. 28. Clindamycin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 30. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of biotin, pantothenic acid, pyridoxine, thiamine, and balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The significance is minor or unknown. 31. Clindamycin and erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate) may decrease the effects of each other through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance is minor or unknown. 32. Food decreases the levels of clindamycin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. The significance is minor or unknown. 33. Letermovir increases the levels of clindamycin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Mipomersen and clindamycin may increase the toxicity of each other. Both drugs have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 35. Nitazoxanide and clindamycin may increase the levels of each other through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Clindamycin and ospemifene may increase the levels of each other through plasma protein binding competition. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
